newsitem.title: USA: US Commerce's Daley optimistic on fast-track bill.
newsitem.headline: US Commerce's Daley optimistic on fast-track bill.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of Commerce William Daley on Monday expressed optimism about winning fast-track trade negotiation authority from Congress.

"I think we will work out a strategy and it will be a difficult fight," Daley told a State Department conference on Latin America. "But I am quite confident that when this battle is engaged, we will be quite successful."
Business leaders have said they are eager for the Clinton administration to propose a fast-track trade negotiation bill to get the process moving forward.

Fast-track legislation would allow U.S. trade officials to negotiate an expansion of the North American Free Trade Agreement to include Chile and other market-opening trade accords without fear the pacts will be revised by Congress.

Daley said the administration currently was involved in negotiations with Congress over a plan to balance the budget. He said a successful outcome of that effort would help strengthen bipartisanship and the hands of those in Congress who support fast-track trade legislation.

U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said administration officials were still in the process of consulting members of Congress to try to forge a bill that will win both Republican and Democratic support. She told reporters following a speech to the group that the consultations were likely to continue for some time.

Democrats and Republicans have been divided over the issue of whether to include labor and environmental issues in trade negotiation authority. Republicans, who control Congress, oppose a broad authority to negotiate those issues.
Mexican Minister of Commerce and Industrial Development Herminio Blanco told the group that his government thought labor and environmental issues were separate from trade issues.
